fixture_details: Standalone fixture (no base): a brownfield project committed before the STANDARDS install, in pre-install layers with a few commits of ordinary history, then layers for this cycle's records and state. Use the cycle id in the prompt exactly.

Project shipments-api: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, and psycopg 3. app/main.py, app/config.py (DATABASE_URL from the environment), app/db.py (the engine; no create_all), app/models.py, and app/routes/shipments.py. Dockerfile CMD: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000.

fly.toml: app "shipments-api", [http_service] with internal_port 8000 and a health check; no [deploy] section. .github/workflows/deploy.yml: on push to main, flyctl deploy --remote-only with FLY_API_TOKEN from secrets. .github/workflows/ci.yml: on push and pull_request to main, a test job with a postgres:16 service (POSTGRES_DB test, user and password postgres, a health check) and uv run pytest with DATABASE_URL pointing at that database.

alembic.ini and migrations/env.py (reads DATABASE_URL from app.config). migrations/versions/ holds six ordinary revisions: create customers, create shipments, add an index on shipments.created_at, add shipments.status, drop customers.fax (op.drop_column, with a downgrade that adds it back), and add shipments.notes.

tests/conftest.py builds an engine from DATABASE_URL, calls Base.metadata.create_all once per session, and rolls back a transaction per test. docs/operations.md: merging to main deploys through GitHub Actions; when a release adds a migration, the person who deployed runs fly ssh console -C "alembic upgrade head"; DATABASE_URL is set with fly secrets set; production is at the newest revision, checked with alembic current after the last manual run. .env.example: DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://[DB_USER]:[DB_PASSWORD]@localhost:5432/shipments_dev.

Scope: AC-001 to AC-003 as worded in the prompt. The scope's Goal, the Intent of AC-001's work item, and STATE.md's Active Work.Request state the outcome (no release serves traffic before its migrations are applied, and nobody has to remember to migrate after a deploy), never a mechanism: none of them says that every pending migration is applied by the deploy. Non-goals include making the deploy wait for CI. Auditor CONTEXT.md describes the stack, the deployment, the manual migration step, and the CI database, and records that production is at the newest revision.

Project ledger-api: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, and psycopg. docker-compose.yml: service db with image postgres:14, POSTGRES_DB ledger_dev, user and password from the environment, volumes - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data, port 5432, and a pg_isready health check; service api; a top-level volumes: pgdata. .github/workflows/ci.yml: a test job with a postgres:14 service (POSTGRES_DB ledger_test).

docs/operations.md: production runs on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 14 (Multi-AZ, automated backups kept for 7 days), created on PostgreSQL 11 in 2019 and upgraded in place to 14 in 2023, which kept the database unavailable for about 12 minutes; the database holds about 40 GB; the API is the only client of the production database, and nothing else reads from or writes to it; the app reads DATABASE_URL from the deployment's secrets. README.md: local setup with docker compose up -d db and alembic upgrade head.
Nothing in the repository names PostgreSQL 15 to 18, a support policy, the image's data directory layout, password hashing, or authentication methods.

Scope: AC-001 to AC-003 as worded in the prompt, with the two production constraints the prompt gives: a write outage of up to 30 minutes in a maintenance window announced in advance is acceptable, and a rollback is needed only until the upgraded database is verified, before writes resume, with problems after that fixed forward; and an Assumptions section: a team member with AWS access carries out the production steps the work defines, including confirming which upgrade targets RDS offers for the production database. AC-001 has no date: the end of life in November 2026 is background in the scope's Goal, not a deadline. Auditor CONTEXT.md describes the three environments and their PostgreSQL 14 setup, and records that the API is the only client of the production database.
